name: Painterly 3D
visualIdentity: Painterly 3D (category: Drawing and Illustration) renders 3D forms with painterly surface marks, controlled color masses, and stylized lighting. Brush direction must follow form, and glossy photorealistic highlights are limited. Explicitly distinct from matte clay-style 3D. Camera moves and poses should reveal the painted treatment without making surface textures crawl.
suitableUses: Explicit: the source names this direction for 3D character, environment, and product-style pieces. Inferred: calm environment showcases, title shots, key art in motion, and illustrated explainers where painted surfaces should read clearly. Pre-rendering in Blender is needed; it suits character or environment pieces, and hybrids suit cinematic hero shots or HTML stories presenting renders.
limitations: Requires Blender pre-rendering for visual construction, so it is not a direct browser-only look. Surface textures must stay locked to geometry during camera moves. Glossy photoreal highlights are not allowed. Suggested combinations advise against rigid symmetry on character acting and busy brushwork behind text. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics.
palette: Example palette, reference-dependent and optional: background #EFE4D1 (main layout ground), foreground #38454A (text and hierarchy), accent_1 #7D9A95 and accent_2 #BB7C65 (decorative fills). Task-supplied or approved reference colors override these. Opaque foreground-on-background contrast is 7.878. Accent fills fail normal text (3.271 and 2.919), so body text belongs on the main background. Gradients are disabled; no hue substitution is permitted.
motionAndInteraction: Motion is governed by the style's camera and pose rules, with brush direction fixed to form. Shared guidance prefers coherent, authored movement, while deliberate cuts and reading holds remain allowed. Optional motion references are conditional: gaze tracking needs eye layers or a rig; orbit needs full geometry or turntable views; dolly and camera orbit need real 3D depth. Interactive delivery may use pointer or scroll, while video must derive state from composition time.
audio: Audio is unspecified by the style and optional; no mandatory layer is assigned. Suggested direction: restrained audio that supports the topic and never competes with narration or essential text. Music may be useful for mood and tempo, and sound accents may clarify key actions or transitions. Silence can support reading holds. Speech intelligibility, balance, and clipping must be verified in the final export.
assetRequirements: Required: Blender for models, materials, lighting, animation, and offline renders; Python bpy run through Blender for procedural scenes; EEVEE or Cycles for rendering. Stable brush textures and stylized materials are needed. Optional: chroma.js for color validation and contrast; HyperFrames as default pipeline, Remotion as conditional fallback. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Assets are unspecified beyond these tools.
combinations: Recommended: style-104 for symmetric, centered hero-shot framing, kept to hero shots only, with the same palette and locked brush texture. Style-019 for editorial typography and layout, with text in #38454A on #EFE4D1 and type never animating faster than the camera. Avoid glossy highlights, crawling textures, and text over busy brushwork. Keep alone for character or environment pieces when no hybrid is needed.
productionApproach: Blender (style_renderer and motion_engine) builds painted materials, lighting, and deterministic keyframed camera and geometry. HyperFrames (default) or Remotion (fallback, with recorded reason) handles scene assembly, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Run npx hyperframes check, snapshot, and render. Inspect opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full decoded video before delivery. Chroma.js is supporting only. Responsibilities are separate.
